title: 2002 AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: According to the standard convention for exponentiation, \[2^{2^{2^2}} = 2^{\left(2^{\left(2^2\right)}\right)} = 2^{16} = 65{,}536.\] If the order in which the exponentiations are performed is changed, how many other values are possible?

solutions.text:
The five parenthesizations of \(2^{2^{2^2}}\) give \[ \begin{aligned} &\left(\left(2^2\right)^2\right)^2 = 2^8, \\ &\left(2^{2^2}\right)^2 = 2^8, \\ &\left(2^2\right)^{2^2} = 2^8, \end{aligned} \] \[2^{\left(2^2\right)^2} = 2^{16},\quad 2^{2^{2^2}} = 2^{16}.\]

So the only values are \(2^{16} = 65{,}536\) and \(2^8 = 256.\) Besides the standard value there is exactly \(1\) other.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: There are five ways to parenthesize a tower of four \(2\)’s
Every parenthesization evaluates to either \(2^{16}\) or \(2^{8}\)
